title: Compact route switcher: live-announcements, keyboard flow, and OS high-contrast mode prototype review
creator: Marco Chen
description: Design review for a compact route-switcher component used in the Console header and rollout flows. This ticket covers an accessibility-first refresh: screen-reader live announcements when routes change, improved single-line compact keyboard navigation, and OS-level high-contrast mode visual tokens. Also includes localization readiness for RTL languages and locale-aware label truncation.
background: The route switcher is newly introduced in several Console routes (Rollouts, Cost Insights, Model Catalog) as a compact control to toggle sub-views. QA flagged inconsistent screen-reader announcements and poor focus order when toggled rapidly. Visual contrast in macOS/Windows high-contrast accessibility modes is inconsistent across tokens. We need a focused design pass and prototype to validate with assistive tech and localized labels.
goals: 1) Ensure screen-reader users receive clear, concise announcements when the route changes and when expanded/collapsed. 2) Keyboard-only users can navigate the switcher using Tab, Enter/Space, and Arrow keys consistently. 3) Visual contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA in both normal and OS high-contrast modes. 4) Component supports RTL and long localized labels without breaking layout.
scope: Design tokens, component markup pattern (ARIA roles, live region usage), keyboard navigation spec, high-contrast color tokens, and Figma prototype for testing with NVDA/VoiceOver/JAWS. Deliverables: annotated component spec, Figma prototype, and checklist for engineering handoff.
out_of_scope: Backend routing logic, analytics instrumentation, and release coordination for individual product pages. Larger header layout changes are not included.
user_stories: As a screen-reader user, I need a concise spoken message when I switch routes so I know the active view.
As a keyboard-only user, I need predictable arrow-key behavior inside the switcher so I can quickly change views.
As a user who enables OS high-contrast, I need the switcher to remain readable and visually distinct.
As an international user, I need the switcher to handle long translated labels and mirror in RTL locales without truncation cutting meaning.
accessibility_checks: Use aria-current on active option and role=tablist/role=tab pattern for consistent semantics
Provide an aria-live=polite live region that announces: 'Switched to <label>.', and separate announcement for 'Switcher collapsed' when closing
Keyboard: Tab enters the switcher, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight moves focus between options, Enter/Space activates. Escape closes if the switcher is a popover
Focus-visible outline must use contrast-safe token and be visible in high-contrast mode
Ensure focus order remains logical when switcher is used inside header with other interactive controls
Test with NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS and with macOS VoiceOver rotor interactions
i18n_checks: Allow multi-line wrapping for labels in narrow widths and provide a max-line clamp fallback with accessible disclosure for truncated labels
Mirror layout for RTL: icons left/right swap, arrow-key directionality inverted where appropriate
Avoid concatenated strings in announcements; use localized full sentences for live region messages
Verify label length hotspots for German, Russian, Japanese — produce examples in Figma
tasks: Finalize annotated component spec with ARIA attributes and live-region copy
Build interactive Figma prototype covering normal, focused, expanded, and high-contrast states
Run first-pass assistive tech testing (Marco + Priya) and document regressions
Update token mapping for high-contrast and publish to design tokens repo
Handoff doc and checklist for engineering (include keyboard matrix and i18n string examples)
acceptance_criteria: Design spec contains explicit ARIA attributes and a single live-region copy pattern for all routes
Prototype demonstrates keyboard flows and arrow-key behavior; test recordings uploaded to Drive
Color token mapping yields contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for text and >= 3:1 for UI components in high-contrast simulations
RTL layout screenshot set provided and verified with mirrored iconography
Engineering has a checklist and has acknowledged feasibility in a comment (ENG lead sign-off)
comments: 2026-02-26 Marco Chen: Initial draft posted. Focus for this sprint: live region language and HC token mapping. Asking Eng for feasibility on using single persistent live region vs ephemeral announcements.
2026-03-01 Priya Nair (A11y): Quick wins noted: prefer aria-live polite, avoid role=status because some screen readers suppress it. I'll run NVDA passes on the prototype Friday.

2026-03-03 Omar Singh (ENG): Feasibility: persistent aria-live region is fine. Concern about rapid firing announcements when users navigate quickly — recommend debounce 300ms on live updates. Also callout: Arrow key semantics must not interfere with global header shortcuts.
2026-03-05 Lina Gomez (PM): Agree on debounce. Please include analytics events for 'switcher_open' and 'switch' as engineering tasks (PM will open ENG-87412).

2026-03-08 Aisha Patel (Designer, assignee): Updated prototype with debounce behavior and additional long-label examples (DE, RU, JA). Added high-contrast token variants and exported screenshots for QA.
2026-03-10 Marco Chen: Reviewers — please test VoiceOver recordings in the Drive folder. I added explicit sample copy for translations to avoid concatenation problems.

2026-03-12 Omar Singh (ENG): Engineering review complete. We can implement with existing header primitives. We'll implement live-region debounce and expose token flags for HC mode. Planning in sprint 2026-03-15 -> ENG implementation PR planned.
notes: Key trade-offs discussed: single live-region vs per-component announcements (single region preferred for clarity). For debounce, we agreed on 300ms but engineering may tune in prod. High-contrast tokens use OS-detection flags mapped to --hc- tokens in CSS.
